newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures drifted lower on Friday as German regional inflation reports and comments from a Bundesbank official dampened hopes for rate cuts although traders said it was a relatively calm decline.

The March bond future slipped 0.46 to 130.32, close to the low for the day reached after German state Baden-Wuerttemberg reported a 0.5 percent rise in prices, pushing the year-on-year rate to 1.7 percent.
Traders said many people had got too long of bond futures during the recent rally and took the opportunity to lighten their positions somewhat.

"There's nothing more. The market remains positive but the German price reports, after the M3 money supply yesterday, cooled slightly hopes that the Bundesbank will cut rates quickly," an analyst said.
March PIBOR suffered from a similar trend, posting its third consecutive decline. It fell to 96.73 from the week's high of 96.82 while June dropped to 96.75 from 96.86 on Wednesday.
A trader at a French brokerage said the March contract had the potential to fall to 96.70 mainly because there were still investors looking to reduce their positions.
"Hopes for a reduction in rates have cooled but the reduction has only been pushed further out. The fundamentals and inflation still argue for a cut," he said.
Expectations early in the day that domestic investors would step into to support the cash market failed to prevent the 10-year spread with German Bunds underperforming slightly.
French yields moved to 17 basis points below German yields compared with 19 on Thursday.
Traders said the bond future could suffer more at the beginning of next week from a further correction, depending largely on what happened in the U.S. bond market.
The contract had slipped to a low of 130.16 late on Friday in GLOBEX trading as the U.S. bond market extended its losses.

The franc remained steady against the mark at 3.3727 per mark compared with 3.3730 on Thursday. Its decline against the dollar continued to reverse. The franc climbed as high as 5.4790 from 5.5065 on Thursday and 5.5470 on Wednesday, the lowest level since July 16, 1994.
